chunks: And he was asked about a man who pays in advance for sheep, two-year-olds and younger ones and other than that, until a specified term. He said:

There is no harm if the one who owes the sheep cannot provide all that he owes: the owner of the sheep may take half of them, or a third of them, or two-thirds of them, and take the capital value of what remains of the sheep in dirhams; and he may take less than their stipulation, but he must not take more than their stipulation.
He said: And garments also are like wheat, barley, saffron, and sheep.

key_terms.أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى: a fixed, specified term for delivery
key_terms.ثُنْيَانٍ: two-year-old animals in this commercial context
key_terms.جُذْعَانٍ: younger animals of a specified age category
key_terms.يُسْلِفُ: to pay in advance in a forward sale arrangement

ai.seo_question: If a seller in an advance purchase contract cannot deliver all the sheep owed, can the buyer take some goods and the rest in dirhams?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on salam-like advance purchase contracts involving sheep and similar goods. If the seller cannot fully deliver the agreed goods, the buyer may accept a portion of the goods and recover the remaining principal in dirhams, so long as he does not take more than what was originally stipulated.
